llm.summary: The skill implements the advertised P2P portal and deployment features, but its metadata, runtime instructions, and code disagree about required secrets and it automates sensitive token exchanges and remote deployment steps—these inconsistencies and automated behaviors merit caution before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name/description (Agent P2P Portal client + Portal deployment) matches the code: it contains a local bridge/client and remote Portal server deployment code. However the registry metadata claims no required environment variables or credentials while the SKILL.md and code clearly require API keys, the OpenClaw hooks token, and (for deployment) an SSH private key. That mismatch between declared requirements and actual implementation is an incoherence worth flagging.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the included client code direct the agent to run local bridge/start scripts and to call local OpenClaw hooks. More concerning: the client automatically parses guest messages for verification codes and tokens, posts confirmation requests to third-party portals, and wakes the main session with messages containing token snippets. That gives the skill broad discretion to read/parse messages, extract secrets (Tokens), and make outgoing HTTP requests on behalf of the user — behavior beyond simple message delivery and therefore risky if not fully audited.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal package install spec in the registry (instruction-only), but a full install/deploy toolset is included (install.py, scripts/deploy_portal.py, etc.). The installer uses paramiko/SSH to deploy to user VPS and can modify remote systemd services and install packages. This remote-deploy approach is expected for a Portal deployer but increases risk because it requires SSH private key access and executes commands on a remote host.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires and uses multiple sensitive values: AGENTP2P_API_KEY, AGENTP2P_HUB_URL, OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL, OPENCLAW_HOOKS_TOKEN and also reads AGENTP2P_TOKEN / SSH private keys during install. These are proportionate for P2P Portal + local Gateway wake logic, but the registry metadata claimed none — an inconsistency. Additional concerns: the code auto-extracts/handles tokens from messages (regex), and the installer writes gateway.env and may set a hard-coded SECRET_KEY in the remote systemd/service manifest. Hard-coded secrets and automated handling of tokens increase the chance of accidental credential exposure.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true. It writes files under the user's home (~/.openclaw and its skill directory) and the installer will create remote services on a VPS if used. Those privileges are consistent with deploying and running a Portal + local bridge. There is no evidence it modifies other skills' configs beyond writing gateway.env/openclaw config as part of setup (which is expected for integration).
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to consider before installing:

- Metadata mismatch: The registry claims no required env vars, but the skill (SKILL.md and code) needs API keys, the OpenClaw hooks token, and — for Portal deployment — your SSH private key. Treat that discrepancy as a red flag; ask the publisher why metadata omits these requirements.

- Secrets & automation: The client automatically parses messages to extract verification codes and tokens and will POST confirmations to external Portal endpoints and wake your OpenClaw session with token snippets. If you give this skill your hooks token or API keys, it could cause tokens to be saved, echoed to logs/notifications, or sent to remote services automatically. Only proceed if you trust the code and understand the automation.

- Deployment requires SSH private key: The included installer will SSH to your VPS and run commands, create systemd services, and install code. Do not supply your private SSH key unless you review the deploy scripts and trust them. Prefer manual deployment (review scripts and run commands yourself on a disposable VM) if you are uncertain.

- Default credentials & hard-coded secret: The docs/config mention default admin passwords and the installer writes a fixed SECRET_KEY into the systemd setup. Change defaults and the SECRET_KEY before exposing the Portal publicly.

- Recommended actions before use:
  - Review these specific files carefully: client.py, install.py, scripts/deploy_portal.py, src/main.py and any code that handles tokens/verification flows.
  - Test in an isolated environment (VM/container) and with non-production credentials first.
  - Don’t provide real SSH keys or production tokens until you audit the deploy script behavior.
  - Change any default admin passwords and replace hard-coded SECRET_KEY values.
  - Consider manual deployment (git clone + inspect + run) instead of running the included one-click installer.

If you want, I can highlight the exact lines that parse/extract tokens and the parts that post confirmations to remote portals, or help you produce a minimal checklist to safely audit the deploy script.
